goal: Determine whether postgres.js max_pipeline=1 eliminates the Connection wedge while preserving sql.begin(), record the result, and leave production clients unchanged when the candidate fails.
non_goals: Change src/lib/db/server.ts or any production postgres.js client configuration.
Claim that max_pipeline=1 fixes the mechanism before the isolated differential runs.
Raise DB_POOL_MAX or DB_READ_POOL_MAX, reroute reads, deploy, or mutate staging or production data.
Close issue 773's Fluid Compute isolate-sharing question from this driver-only experiment.
Capture the authenticated staging latency baseline in this investigation after max_pipeline=1 is rejected; the future capacity-treatment feature owns that pre-change measurement.
user_visible_behavior: No customer-facing behavior changes in this investigation.
Maintainers receive conclusive evidence distinguishing depth-1-clean, depth-1-wedged, and inconclusive outcomes without risking a production client.
invariants: Production postgres.js clients retain their current options and max_pipeline default.
The differential runs only against a positively confirmed ephemeral Supabase branch and preserves its terminate-all cleanup barrier.
The legacy max_pipeline=100 arm remains an explicit negative control even if production defaults later change.
A live local test proves max_pipeline=1 still permits sql.begin() to reserve and commit before the configuration can be considered a candidate.
No production or staging schema, tenant scope, authorization, durable data, or external environment configuration changes; any execution deviation on a disposable branch is recorded explicitly.
edge_cases: A depth-1 wedge is a conclusive rejection of this approach, not a tooling failure.
A fulfilled depth-1 arm is candidate evidence only; it does not prove cross-request isolate behavior or staging latency.
Rejected or hung-unknown experiment arms are inconclusive and exit nonzero.
The postgres.js max_pipeline option is absent from its TypeScript Options interface, so the harness uses a narrow local compatibility cast and protects behavior with a live sql.begin() test.

The authenticated staging latency protocol remains mandatory before a future production capacity treatment is proposed or deployed, so later comparison uses the identical route, auth state, cache state, concurrency, and full-body timing.
